strengths: Strong empirical results achieving state-of-the-art on Design-Bench benchmarks with consistent improvements across tasks and rigorous evaluation over 8 random seeds
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including 15+ baselines, extensive ablations on key components, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Well-motivated and clearly presented methodology with thoughtful three-stage training pipeline combining domain adaptation, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning
Broad applicability demonstrated across discrete sequence design (DNA) and continuous control (robot morphology) domains
Good reproducibility practices with detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, training time estimates, and code release promise
weaknesses: Critical gap between stated motivation and validation: the main claim about bidirectional modeling advantages is never empirically demonstrated; no direct comparison with comparable AR baseline or analysis showing diffusion LLMs actually leverage bidirectional dependencies better than alternatives

Severe performance dependency on similarity-conditioned context construction (Table 4: 0.235 drop on TF8 without it) suggests method succeeds through local search rather than stated bidirectional modeling capability—this fundamental design choice contradicts the motivation

Several unjustified design decisions lacking ablations: omitting reward centering 'to preserve prompt-specific information' contradicts RL theory; omitting KL regularization 'for stability' is non-standard; one-step log-prob approximation used without comparing to full diffusion sampling

Limited technical novelty: delimiter tokens for domain adaptation is incremental, one-step log-prob approximation is from prior work, and standard RL objectives are applied; main contribution is engineering combination of existing techniques rather than fundamental innovation

Narrow experimental scope limited to 4 Design-Bench tasks (2 discrete 8-10D sequences, 2 continuous 56-60D morphologies) with no diversity in application domains (materials, proteins) despite being mentioned in motivation; generalization claims unsupported

Comparison fairness issues: dLLM baseline uses npool=10 vs. 500 for DiBO; OPRO instantiation may not be optimal; lack of significance tests; underperformance on D'Kitty morphology (0.923 vs 0.950 best baseline)

Insufficient analysis and insights: no visualization of generated sequences, no failure case analysis, no explanation of why method outperforms baselines beyond unvalidated bidirectional hypothesis, no ablation on joint vs. separate prompt/response optimization in DA vs. SFT
Incomplete reward signal design: simple label improvement reward (y(o) - max(y(prompt))) is crude; balancing positive/negative rewards in RL lacks justification; no analysis of reward signal quality

strengths: Well-motivated core idea: bidirectional dependencies in design problems are compelling, with clear validation through matched diffusion vs. AR comparison showing consistent gains especially on discrete tasks (0.080 on TF Bind 8)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 14+ baseline comparisons spanning diverse method classes, tests on 4 Design-Bench tasks plus RNA variants, strong results on 3/4 main tasks with substantial improvements (0.101 on TF Bind 8)
Thorough ablation studies systematically validating each component: delimiter tokens, training stages, context similarity, hyperparameters, all showing clear necessity

Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, 8-seed reporting with standard deviations, complete prompt templates, pretraining-overlap audit confirming no task-specific knowledge in pretrained model, code availability promised
Honest discussion of limitations and failure modes: acknowledges underperformance on D'Kitty and mixed RNA results rather than overclaming generality

Sound technical execution: joint prompt-response loss well-motivated for domain adaptation, similarity-conditioned context selection validated, reasonable uniform policy assumption for offline RL with clear justification
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily engineers existing techniques together (delimiter tokens, standard SFT+RL) rather than introducing algorithmically novel contributions; each component is straightforward design choice

Mixed and task-dependent results: underperforms on D'Kitty Morphology (-0.027 vs best baseline), mixed RNA results with failure on RNA-B (0.299 vs ExPT 0.348), and modest continuous task improvements (0.011-0.042) often within standard deviation ranges
Insufficient analysis of failure modes: no investigation into why D'Kitty underperforms or RNA-B fails; lacks error analysis showing which design types struggle

Design choice justifications need more validation: one-step RL approximation (Eq. 6) lacks ablation vs. full denoising; reward dataset construction strategy detailed only in appendix with potential distribution shift risk

Scalability and scope limitations: all experiments use fixed n_pool=500 with unclear scaling to realistic 10K+ sample datasets; context length capped at 7 examples due to H100 GPU memory; only Design-Bench tasks comprehensively evaluated

Limited theoretical analysis of when/why bidirectional modeling helps: while gains larger for discrete (DNA: 0.080) than continuous (Ant: 0.018) tasks, deeper investigation of the underlying mechanisms would strengthen claims

strengths: Clear and well-motivated use of diffusion LLMs for bidirectional context modeling in design problems with strong intuition for why this addresses AR limitations
Rigorous matched comparison between diffusion and AR backbones (Table 2) isolating the contribution of bidirectional modeling, showing consistent gains especially on discrete tasks (+0.050-0.080)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 14+ baselines, multiple evaluation metrics (100th percentile, Top-K, median), 8 random seeds, and additional RNA tasks for generalization testing
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, dataset construction procedures, prompt templates, pretraining-overlap audit (Table 12), and promised code availability
Thorough ablation studies strategically isolating each component (delimiter tokens, training stages, context construction, hyperparameters) with clear evidence of necessity
State-of-the-art or competitive overall performance: rank mean 2.5, median rank 1.0 across Design-Bench tasks with substantial gains on DNA tasks (TF Bind 8: +0.101 over best baseline)
Technically sound three-stage pipeline balancing coarse (SFT) and fine-grained (RL) feedback with efficient one-step log-probability approximation
Honest limitations discussion and impact statement acknowledging potential risks and mixed results on certain tasks
weaknesses: Inconsistent performance across tasks: underperforms ExPT on D'Kitty Morphology (0.923 vs 0.950) and shows mixed results on RNA tasks (loses substantially on RNA-B and Top-K metrics), raising questions about generalization

Lacks theoretical or analytical justification for when bidirectional modeling helps: gains on continuous tasks (0.015-0.018) much smaller than discrete (0.050-0.080) without deep analysis of task characteristics driving this difference

Design choices appear ad-hoc or insufficiently justified: delimiter tokens lack comparison to alternatives, RL assumes uniform old policy without ablation, greedy decoding strategy not compared to sampling, reward normalization rationale unclear
Statistical significance not formally evaluated despite large standard deviations relative to some improvements (e.g., Grad-EI vs DiBO on D'Kitty both ~0.923)
Computational cost not addressed: no comparison of training/inference time with baselines despite three-stage pipeline; iterative denoising vs single-pass AR generation time not analyzed
Limited exploration of true small-data regime: focus on n_pool=500; performance at critically scarce data (n_pool <100) and scalability to larger datasets unexplored
Incomplete analysis of design quality beyond scores: no evaluation of diversity, validity rates, or plausibility of generated designs despite these being critical for real-world applications

RL approximation validity not thoroughly tested: one-step unmasking (Eq. 6) may lose inter-token dependencies crucial to diffusion, but full denoising alternative not explored; uniform old policy assumption not ablated
Missing ablation on training stage necessity: Table 4 shows DA+SFT outperforms DA+RL substantially, but minimal exploration of whether DA or individual stages can be omitted

Comparison with concurrent diffusion LLM work (dLLM, Yuan et al. 2026) excluded from main evaluation due to different experimental settings, preventing direct assessment of training-based vs inference-only approaches
